title: Microsoft Purview: auto-labeling ceiling for SharePoint and OneDrive rises to 500,000 files a day (Worldwide)
summary: The briefing passes: the automatic capacity increase, licensing examples and all eight control surfaces are supported. The statement that simulation is the only documented checkpoint is broader than the documentation establishes, and the encryption settings named in the checklist have no controls-table row.

claims.claim: This is a Microsoft Purview Information Protection auto-labeling change.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview: Information Protection - Auto-labeling scale increase for SharePoint and OneDrive

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The SharePoint and OneDrive maximum increases from 100,000 to up to 500,000 files per tenant per day.
claims.quote: We are increasing the maximum auto-labeling capacity for SharePoint and OneDrive from 100,000 up to 500,000 files per tenant per day.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends creating a policy in simulation mode for organisations not currently using auto-labeling.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends reviewing simulation results before enabling a policy.
claims.quote: Review simulation results to validate expected labeling outcomes.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends enabling the policy after validation.
claims.quote: Enable the policy after validation to take advantage of the increased daily processing limit.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Learn describes 500,000 as absolute maximum daily throughput aggregated across all auto-labeling policies in the tenant.
claims.quote: The absolute maximum throughput is 500,000 automatically labeled SharePoint and OneDrive files per tenant per day, in aggregate across all auto-labeling policies.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The ceiling is not a guaranteed or consistently expected daily processing rate.
claims.quote: This ceiling isn't a guaranteed or consistently expected daily processing rate; actual throughput can be lower.

claims.claim: Actual auto-labeling throughput can be lower than the ceiling.
claims.quote: This ceiling isn't a guaranteed or consistently expected daily processing rate; actual throughput can be lower.

claims.claim: The same capacity increase has a separate roadmap item, 571309, with status Launched.
claims.quote: 571309: "status": "Launched"; "description": "We are increasing the maximum auto-labeling capacity for SharePoint and OneDrive from 100,000 up to 500,000 files per tenant per day."

claims.claim: Roadmap item 571309 targets November CY2026.
claims.quote: 571309: "targetDate": "November CY2026"

claims.claim: Roadmap item 571309 lists GCC, GCC High and DoD.
claims.quote: 571309: "clouds": [ "GCC", "GCC High", "DoD" ]

claims.claim: Auto-labeling policies run continuously until deleted.
claims.quote: Auto-labeling policies run continuously until they're deleted.

claims.claim: New and modified files are included with current policy settings.
claims.quote: For example, new and modified files will be included with the current policy settings.

claims.claim: The roadmap frames faster labeling as preparation for Microsoft 365 Copilot.
claims.quote: With sensitivity labels and protection settings applied to more files sooner, organizations can better prepare their data estate for Microsoft 365 Copilot with greater confidence.

claims.claim: No documented effect of this ceiling increase changes a tenant that has no auto-labeling policies.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview auto-labeling higher capacity 500000 tenant no policies automatic default configuration; opened apply-sensitivity-label-automatically; read default-sensitivity-labels-policies search excerpts and MC1461154. Default-policy creation is separate from this ceiling increase.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A label applying encryption through a SharePoint or OneDrive auto-labeling policy must use Assign permissions now.
claims.quote: When the auto-labeling policy includes locations for SharePoint or OneDrive, the label must be configured for the Assign permissions now setting, and User access to content expires must be set to Never.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: For those encrypted labels, User access to content expires must be Never.
claims.quote: When the auto-labeling policy includes locations for SharePoint or OneDrive, the label must be configured for the Assign permissions now setting, and User access to content expires must be set to Never.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Label encryption restricts access to authorised users, so people without rights cannot read the protected content.
claims.quote: Can be decrypted only by users authorized by the label's encryption settings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: An auto-labeling policy can replace a lower-priority manually applied label when the override setting is chosen.
claims.quote: All locations: Applicable for emails and for files in SharePoint and OneDrive. When you select this setting, an existing sensitivity label will always be overriden if the sensitivity label you chose for the policy has a higher priority.

claims.claim: A removal policy can remove the selected label even if it was manually applied.
claims.quote: For SharePoint and OneDrive, an auto-labeling policy configured to automatically remove a label can remove the selected label, including when the label was manually applied, and leave the content unlabeled.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Turning a policy from Ready to turn on to On requires Compliance Administrator or Compliance Data Administrator.
claims.quote: Turning a policy from Ready to turn on to On requires Compliance Administrator or Compliance Data Administrator. Without one of these roles, the Turn on policy button appears greyed out even after a successful simulation.

claims.claim: An active service-side policy labels content without user interaction.
claims.quote: Because the user doesn't interact with the labeling process, auto-labeling policies don't support recommended labeling

claims.claim: A policy must run at least one simulation before automatically applying or removing labels.
claims.quote: You can't automatically label documents and emails, or remove labels, until your policy has run at least one simulation.

claims.claim: Simulation is the only documented checkpoint before the service acts.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview auto-labeling simulation only checkpoint before policy actions prerequisites validation; read apply-sensitivity-label-automatically, auto-label-simulation-results and troubleshooting excerpts. They require simulation but do not state this exclusive description.
claims.fix: Remove 'Simulation is the only documented checkpoint before the service acts.' Keep the preceding, supported statement that the policy must run at least one simulation.

claims.claim: Files cannot be auto-labeled while open.
claims.quote: Files can't be auto-labeled if they're part of an open session (the file is open).

claims.claim: PDFs are skipped unless PDF labeling is enabled for the tenant.
claims.quote: If PDF labeling isn't enabled, PDFs are skipped entirely: PDFs aren't evaluated or sent for labeling, and no label is applied.

claims.claim: PDF and Word, Excel and PowerPoint files are supported.
claims.quote: PDF documents and Office files for Word (.docx), PowerPoint (.pptx), and Excel (.xlsx) are supported.

claims.claim: A OneDrive account not associated with its corresponding user account is unsupported.
claims.quote: A OneDrive account that isn't associated with its user account (sometimes called a detached OneDrive account) isn't supported for auto-labeling or simulation.

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels must be enabled for Office files in SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labels are enabled for Office files in SharePoint and OneDrive. Required before any label can be applied to files in those locations.

claims.claim: The maximum is 100 auto-labeling policies per tenant.
claims.quote: Maximum of 100 auto-labeling policies per tenant.

claims.claim: The Auto-labeling page is not visible where its backend Azure dependency is unsupported.
claims.quote: Auto-labeling isn't currently available in all regions because of a backend Azure dependency. If your tenant can't support this functionality, the Auto-labeling page isn't visible in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Client and service-side automatic sensitivity labeling is included with Microsoft 365 E5, supporting the included licensing model for this existing capability's ceiling increase.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5, Microsoft Purview Suite/GOV/FLW, Microsoft Defender + Purview Suite FLW, Microsoft 365 E5 Information Protection and Governance | Office 365 E5/A5/G5; Client and service-side automatic sensitivity labeling | Included | Included

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The feature matrix includes service-side automatic sensitivity labeling with Microsoft 365 E5 Information Protection and Governance.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5, Microsoft Purview Suite/GOV/FLW, Microsoft Defender + Purview Suite FLW, Microsoft 365 E5 Information Protection and Governance | Office 365 E5/A5/G5; Client and service-side automatic sensitivity labeling | Included | Included

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The auto-labeling page directs service-side entitlement checks to the Client and service-side automatic sensitivity labeling matrix entry.
claims.quote: Check the Client and service-side automatic sensitivity labeling entry in the feature matrix linked below. Client-only entitlements don't establish service-side entitlement.

claims.claim: E3 or Business Premium manual labeling entitlement does not include automatic labeling; an eligible subscription or add-on must be checked in the matrix.
claims.quote: You have E3 or Business Premium. Manual labeling entitlement doesn't include automatic labeling. Check the feature matrix for an eligible subscription or add-on for the labeling method you intend to use.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate charge, meter or licence for the increased daily ceiling is documented in November 2026 or mentioned in the roadmap and supplied notice.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview auto-labeling scale increase 500000 pricing separate charge license meter; Purview billing auto-labeling SharePoint OneDrive price 500000. Read auto-labeling guidance, Purview service-description licensing tables, roadmap and MC1461154; no ceiling-specific charge found.

claims.claim: Viewing file contents in simulation source view needs Data Classification Content Viewer.
claims.quote: To view file or email contents in the source view, you must have the Data Classification Content Viewer role

claims.claim: Global admins do not hold Data Classification Content Viewer by default.
claims.quote: Global admins don't have this role by default.

claims.claim: The location-editing route is Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > Edit policy > Choose locations where you want to apply the label.
claims.quote: Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies; select the Edit policy option at the top of the page, from either tab; Choose locations where you want to apply the label: Select and specify locations for Exchange, SharePoint, and OneDrive.

claims.claim: Security & Compliance PowerShell supports Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity <PolicyIdParameter> -AddSharePointLocation <SharePointSites> to add included sites.
claims.quote: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy [-Identity] <PolicyIdParameter> ... [-AddSharePointLocation <MultiValuedProperty>]; The AddSharePointLocation parameter specifies the SharePoint sites to add to the list of included sites ... You identify the site by its URL value.

claims.claim: AddOneDriveLocation is the corresponding parameter for adding OneDrive sites.
claims.quote: The AddOneDriveLocation parameter specifies the OneDrive sites to add to the list of included sites when you aren't using the value All for the OneDriveLocation parameter. You identify the site by its URL value.

claims.claim: Keeping All is exempt from the portal's 1,000 explicitly selected SharePoint-site maximum.
claims.quote: In the portal, each policy can target up to 1,000 explicitly included or excluded SharePoint sites, or up to 100 explicitly included or excluded OneDrive individual users or groups. If you keep the default configuration of All, this configuration is exempt from these maximums.

claims.claim: The activation route is Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > Turn on policy.
claims.quote: Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies; Select your policy to see the details of the configuration and status; When you're ready to run the policy without simulation, select the Turn on policy option.

claims.claim: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity <PolicyIdParameter> -Mode Enable enables policy actions in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell. Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy [-Identity] <PolicyIdParameter> ... [-Mode <PolicyMode>]; Enable: The policy is enabled for actions and notifications.

claims.claim: Mode TestWithoutNotifications is the test or simulation mode.
claims.quote: TestWithoutNotifications: An audit mode where no actions are taken, and no notifications are sent (Test mode).

claims.claim: Mode Disable turns off the policy.
claims.quote: Disable: The policy is disabled.

claims.claim: Per-policy review is at Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > View details, with Labeled items and Labeling failures tabs.
claims.quote: Go to Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies. Select a policy, then select View details in the policy details panel. ... The newer review page has separate Overview, Labeled items, and Labeling failures tabs.

claims.claim: Export-ActivityExplorerData -Filter1 @("Activity", "LabelApplied") exports labeling activity using Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell. ... The Filter1 parameter filters the data to export. ... For example, @("Activity", "LabelApplied") returns records with the activity value LabelApplied.

claims.claim: The export and per-policy review pages are distinct monitoring views rather than operations that change the ceiling.
claims.quote: Use the Export-ActivityExplorerData cmdlet to export activities from Data classification > Activity Explorer in the Microsoft 365 Purview compliance portal.

claims.claim: Auditing for Microsoft 365 must be on for auto-labeling simulation.
claims.quote: Simulation mode: Auditing for Microsoft 365 must be turned on.

claims.claim: Auditing can be enabled at Microsoft Purview portal > Audit > Start recording user and admin activity.
claims.quote: Select the Audit solution card. ... If auditing isn't turned on for your organization, a banner is displayed prompting you to start recording user and admin activity. Select the Start recording user and admin activity banner.

claims.claim: Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true enables auditing in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: Connect to Exchange Online PowerShell. Run the following PowerShell command to turn on auditing. Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true

claims.claim: Turning auditing on or off requires the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online to turn auditing on or off.

claims.claim: The auditing activation banner appears when auditing is not already on.
claims.quote: If auditing isn't turned on for your organization, a banner is displayed prompting you to start recording user and admin activity.

claims.claim: Activity explorer export requires assigned Security & Compliance PowerShell permissions.
claims.quote: To use this cmdlet in Security & Compliance PowerShell, you need to be assigned permissions.

claims.claim: Activity explorer reports on up to 30 days of data.
claims.quote: Activity explorer reports on up to 30 days worth of data.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Learn's policy labeling-progress figures update every 48 hours.
claims.quote: This progress information updates every 48 hours, so you can expect to see the most current data about every other day.

claims.claim: The separate policy-simulation limit is 20,000,000 matched files.
claims.quote: Simulation mode supports up to 20,000,000 matched files. ... This maximum of 20,000,000 matched files applies to simulation mode only and not to an auto-labeling policy that's already turned on to apply sensitivity labels.

claims.claim: Every control that the governance checklist tells administrators to check is represented in the controls table.
claims.quote: Checklist: Check every label ... Assign permissions now ... User access to content expires ... Never. Table rows: policy locations; policy mode; labeling monitoring; unified audit logging. No label-encryption settings row.
claims.fix: The Before rollout step checking Assign permissions now and User access to content expires has no controls-table row. Remove that checklist bullet; retain the supported encryption prerequisites in Risk assessment. Do not add a new row as part of this correction.
